note: Braids' TIMBRE is the decay and its COLOR drives the noise cutoff/harmonics gain/noise-mode crossfade together, so p1 maps to the engine's TIMBRE and p2 to its HARMONICS. MORPH and MACRO sit at noon in every case (Spread 1.0 = the module's own six-partial voicing exactly; Decay spread 1.0 = the module's own per-partial divergence exactly). DRUM is a one-shot per trigger, so every case drives triggerHz > 0 and seconds is an exact multiple of the hit period, giving both sides the SAME number of hits in the compared window -- triggerHz 0 would leave the port silent (TRIGGER_UNPATCHED, never a rising edge; see render_model.cc:91-99) while the Braids reference still strikes once at t=0. The five note-45 cases declare no cents tolerance: ab_engine.py's autocorrelation f0 tracker locks onto exactly 2000 Hz (its own upper search bound, min_lag = rate/f_max) on BOTH sides at that register, a degenerate 'hit the search wall' result, not a pitch reading -- confirmed by comparing raw (uncorrected) f0 directly with ab_compare.py, which prints 'reference 2000.00 Hz  port 2000.00 Hz' verbatim. Six simultaneous partials (two sharing the fundamental, four inharmonic overtones) plus two of them ring-modulated by noise give the single-lag autocorrelator nothing reliable to lock onto at note 45, the same caveat particle-burst's header documents for its own multi-resonator chord. high-register (note 72) is the exception and DOES track: raw f0 reads 524.76 Hz reference against 526.26 Hz port (+4.95 cents raw, +0.3 cents after the kCorrectedSampleRate subtraction) -- close to the note's nominal 523.25 Hz on both sides, so that ONE case keeps a real cents tolerance as the suite's positive pitch check; the per-band tables (run with --bands) cover the fundamental at note 45 instead, where every case's dominant band matches within 0.2 dB. color-dark is deliberately an EIGHT-hit, four-second window like the other multi-hit cases even though COLOR 0 is where the noise lowpass is slowest (cutoff coefficient ~45/32768, a multi-hundred-millisecond three-stage memory that a strike never resets): the chain's integer truncation is reproduced (see struck_drum_engine.h, NOISE-CHAIN TRUNCATION), so its behaviour is dominated by Braids' own deterministic DC offset rather than by the RNG sequence, and the long window no longer accumulates a difference. Measured: +0.03 dB over eight hits. Before that truncation was reproduced the same window read +2.32 dB and grew with length (2 hits +1.61 dB), which is exactly the signature to re-check here if this case ever regresses.
